newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Zhuhai official denies rumours on highway bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Zhuhai official denies rumours on highway bond issue.

text.p: A senior government official from the southern Chinese special economic zone of Zhuhai issued a statement on Tuesday denying a report in a Hong Kong newspaper which said a recent project bond issued for the city did not receive clearance from Chinese authorities.
A Hong Kong newspaper had earlier reported the issue had been improperly guaranteed by state tax revenues and was launched without all of the necessary government approvals.

"The Zhuhai Highway Company bond issue was formally approved by the State Administration for Exchange Control (SAEC), which is the central government regulator for foreign exchange and foreign debt," Cai Guangcheng, vice mayor of the City of Zhuhai, said in a statement issued in Hong Kong.
He said the SAEC had reported its final approval to the People's Bank of China after examining the structure and terms of the transaction.
The Zhuhai government also reported the transaction to the State Planning Commission and other relevant authorities of the central government, Cai said.
The US$200 million bond, which was offered to U.S. investors in August via lead manager Morgan Stanley, was hailed by bankers as a landmark infrastructure financing transaction for China.

The non-recourse bond was secured by annual levies on all of Zhuhai's local vehicles and by entry tolls imposed on all non-local vehicles. Proceeds of the bond are to be used for various infrastructure projects in Zhuhai.
Cai denied suggestions that the revenues used to back the bonds were government tax revenues and therefore could not be used as security.

"The annual usage fees and entry tolls payable to Zhuhai Highway Co are operating revenues of the four Sino-foreign joint ventures from which Zhuhai Highway Co leased the operating rights of the Zhuhai Highway," he said.
Therefore, dedication of these revenues to the servicing of the Zhuhai bond issue is not subject to regulatory restrictions, he said.
Cai said the bond issue was carefully reviewed for compliance with current Chinese laws and regulations by Chinese and international counsels.
He also said the the Zhuhai government has not received any indication of non-compliance from the central government.
